priced_in_summary: Not TOO_LATE, and the reason it is not is worth stating because the surface facts point that way. A +37.35% twelve-month move that is 100% multiple expansion on falling revenue and falling net income, with the price 0.72% under its 52-week high and at the sell-side average target, is the textbook shape of a re-rating that ate its runway (method section 2). What stops this dive calling it is that the multiple expanded against real new forward numbers rather than against a story: H1 2026 group order intake +25.2% to 5.9bn EUR, order backlog a record 12,602.1 MEUR (+20.5% versus year-end 2025, or 1.60x FY2025 revenue), Hydropower intake 2,445.9 MEUR in six months against 2,516.1 MEUR for the whole of record-year 2025. For a plant engineer the order book IS the estimate revision, so the decomposition method section 7 demands does not show story-over-numbers; it shows a multiple that moved because the forward numbers moved. That is ordinary correct pricing, and the verdict for correct pricing is WATCH, not TOO_LATE.

bull.point: The order book moved harder than anything in the P&L, and for a long-cycle plant engineer the order book is the forward estimate. H1 2026 group order intake rose 25.2% to 5.9 billion EUR, the order backlog reached a record 12,602.1 MEUR, +20.5% against year-end 2025 and 1.60x FY2025 revenue of 7,883.1 MEUR, and Hydropower order intake alone was 2,445.9 MEUR, +81.8% against 1,345.4 MEUR in H1 2025 and within 3% of the whole of FY2025's own record 2,516.1 MEUR in half the time. That is contracted work, not a forecast.

bear.point: The money corner is the group's lowest-margin business, so converting the record hydro backlog shifts mix AGAINST group margin. Hydropower earned a 6.5% EBITA margin in 2025 against a group 8.2%. Size the whole thesis at its own disclosed margin: Hydropower revenue DOUBLING from 1,729.5 MEUR to about 3,459 MEUR by 2030 adds roughly 112 MEUR of EBITA, against roughly 134 MEUR of extra annual free cash flow the current price already asks for by 2030 (454.6M compounding at the implied 5.3% reaches 588.5M). The single most favourable realistic outcome for the money corner does not on its own clear the bar the price has already set, and no service or aftermarket share of hydro revenue is disclosed anywhere to argue the margin improves as it converts.

expectations_gap.denominator: 5 of 5 required rows populated. Market-implied column: 2 of 5 rows carry a number from the solve (revenue_cagr_5y as the FCF-CAGR proxy, terminal), 2 are explicitly NULL because the filed solve does not decompose them (operating_margin, reinvestment_return), and net_gap_direction is a direction rather than a level. Tags across the table: 4 INFERRED, 1 SPECULATIVE, 2 NULL on the market-implied side. The table is not complete in the sense of every cell filled, and saying which cells are empty is the point of this field.
expectations_gap.category_mismatch_note: Stated up front because this analyst's own red team has landed on it twice, on MYRG and on HUBB: quality.reverse_dcf solves a FREE CASH FLOW CAGR, and the required row is a REVENUE CAGR. They are not the same quantity and this file does not pretend they are. Row 1 therefore carries the solve as a labelled proxy and this dive additionally builds its own FCF-CAGR-equivalent (5.49%) in net_gap_direction from its own revenue and margin rows, so the comparison that decides the verdict is like for like.

rows.market_implied_note: This is the solved FCF CAGR, not a decomposed revenue CAGR; the file does not separate them. Carried here as the closest available proxy and named as such.
rows.why: Built rather than asserted: Hydropower revenue of 1,729.5 MEUR compounding at 13% a year to about 3,186 MEUR by 2030, and the other three business areas (6,153.6 MEUR combined) at 1.5%, their own trailing group rate, giving 9,815.7 MEUR against 7,883.1 MEUR, a 4.48% CAGR. That sits above the company's own trailing three-year revenue CAGR of 1.48% and above the midpoint of its FY2026 guide (8.0 to 8.3bn EUR is +1.5% to +5.3%, midpoint +3.4%), and it is deliberately below the 12.5% Hydropower growth of 2025 because a 20.5% six-month backlog step-up converts over years, not immediately. 70th percentile against this issuer's own four-year record, in which revenue peaked at 8,660.0 MEUR in 2023 and has fallen since.
rows.structural_reason: A record 12,602.1 MEUR order backlog at 1.60x annual revenue, and a Hydropower order book that took in 2,445.9 MEUR in one half against 2,516.1 MEUR in all of 2025. Backlog is contracted work, which is a structurally different basis for a growth assumption than a demand forecast.
rows.leading_indicator: FY2026 revenue landing inside the guided 8.0 to 8.3 billion EUR range at the Q1-Q3 2026 and FY2026 releases (watch_triggers[0]).

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose a margin path from the headline FCF CAGR. Recorded NULL rather than invented.
rows.why: This dive underwrites the 8.6% comparable EBITA margin ANDRITZ actually DELIVERED in H1 2026, held flat, and declines to underwrite the 8.7% to 9.1% it GUIDES. The reason is the thesis's own mechanics: the segment carrying it, Hydropower, earned a 6.5% EBITA margin in 2025 against a group 8.2%, so the mix shift the bull case needs is margin-dilutive at group level, and no service or aftermarket share of hydro revenue is disclosed to argue otherwise. 8.6% is nonetheless already the best half-year comparable margin this dive has evidence for (H1 2025: 8.3%; FY2025: 8.2%), which is why 78 and not 50. Definitional caveat, recorded rather than smoothed: the vendor operating margin on the same FY2025 is 7.43%, 77bp below the 8.2% EBITA margin, so this row is stated on the EBITA basis the company reports and is not directly comparable to the vendor field of the same name.
rows.structural_reason: Multi-year price and productivity programmes plus a service tail are the standard case for margin expansion here, and this dive does NOT claim them: no disclosed service share exists in the material on disk. The structural fact that IS evidenced runs the other way, toward dilution as hydro grows into the mix.
rows.leading_indicator: Nine-month 2026 comparable EBITA margin at or above the 8.7% guided floor (watch_triggers[1]) would falsify this row's caution directly.

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose a reinvestment return, and no company-disclosed ROIC or ROCE figure appears in any source read this run. Recorded NULL rather than invented.
rows.why: A crude FY2025 return on invested capital, computed here and not disclosed, is about 16.2%: net income 456.3M over invested capital of 2,815.3M (long-term debt 363.6M plus equity 2,451.7M). Net income is used as the NOPAT proxy deliberately, so that no tax rate is assumed anywhere in this file. The number is flattered by the business model: ANDRITZ runs on large customer advances, so current liabilities of 4,887.7M sit against current assets of 5,514.0M and the invested capital denominator is small. The forward 14% is a deliberate decay below that, because hydro converts at a 6.5% segment margin and because the advance-funded working capital that produces the flattery is the same item this file cannot see (see earnings_quality: contract liabilities are absent from the vendor aggregate).
rows.leading_indicator: FY2026 receivables days against the 59.52 of FY2025: a third consecutive rise would say the advance-funded working-capital position is weakening, which is what would compress this return in practice.

rows.why: No disagreement, and saying so is worth a row. 2.5% perpetual growth sits at or below the long-run nominal GDP ceiling this repo's base rates cite, and it is the one input this dive would not move for a European capital-goods engineer. The assumption this dive WOULD question is the other one, and it cannot: the 9% discount rate is high for a EUR-denominated net-cash industrial, and a lower rate would LOWER the implied CAGR and therefore WIDEN this dive's own gap in its own favour. Method section 7 forbids re-solving in session, so the direction is stated and the number is not touched. This is the same shape as the base-FCF sensitivity finding already recorded in the dive log on 2026-08-31: the file publishes a horizon sensitivity and no discount-rate sensitivity.

rows.note: The comparison, made like for like rather than revenue-against-FCF. Carrying this dive's own rows forward: revenue 9,815.7 MEUR in 2030 at a comparable EBITA margin held flat at 8.6% gives EBITA of 844.2 MEUR against 646.4 MEUR in 2025 (7,883.1 at 8.2%), a 5.49% CAGR, and at unchanged cash conversion that is this dive's FCF-CAGR-equivalent expectation. Against the filed 5-year market-implied 5.3%, the gap is +0.19 percentage points. The file's own horizon_spread is 1.21 percentage points. Method section 7 is explicit: a gap inside the band is not a gap. At the 10-year convention the implied number is 4.09% and the same 5.49% expectation is +1.40pp ahead, which IS wider than the spread, so the SIGN of the finding depends on which convention is read, and section 7 requires a dive to say which it claims. This dive claims the filed 5-year default, and therefore claims NO measurable gap. It does not get to claim the 10-year reading here and the 5-year reading elsewhere. That is the whole verdict: the expectations gap the screen sent this dive to find closed on 2026-07-30, and what is left is inside the file's own error bar.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: On the headline price this dive has no material disagreement with consensus, and that IS the primary finding: the stock trades at the 6-analyst average 12-month target of 82.833 EUR and this dive's own build lands 0.19 percentage points from the price's implied ask, inside the file's 1.21-point horizon spread. The one specific, falsifiable disagreement that remains is about MARGIN, not growth: the market and the company read the record Hydropower order book as consistent with FY2026 comparable EBITA margin of 8.7% to 9.1%, and this dive expects it to land at or below the 8.7% floor, because Hydropower earns 6.5% EBITA against a group 8.2%, so the mix shift the order book creates dilutes group margin rather than expanding it, and H1 2026 already printed 8.6%, under the floor.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: A composition error, and a small one, which is why it supports WATCH rather than a call. Order intake and backlog are reported in euros of revenue with no margin attached, so a record Hydropower book reads as an unambiguous positive when the segment carrying it is the group's least profitable. Separately and further upstream, a framing error this dive corrects rather than inherits: the chain scored crowdedness 30 on the observation that nobody frames Andritz as a Medog beneficiary, which is true, and the screen then carried it forward as though it described the security's ownership and attention, which it does not. 5 of 6 analysts rate it Buy and it repriced 9.43% in a session on its own numbers.
independence_test.falsification: Stated to prove this dive WRONG, not to confirm it, the polarity error this analyst's repairs log has now caught twice (VRT 2026-08-29, HUBB 2026-09-02). At the Q1-Q3 2026 release, expected late October or early November 2026 on the company's own cadence (H1 published 2026-07-30), if nine-month comparable EBITA margin comes in AT OR ABOVE 8.7%, the floor of the company's own guide, while revenue tracks inside the guided 8.0 to 8.3 billion EUR range, then the margin-dilution reasoning behind this dive's operating_margin row and its bear case is wrong: the guided expansion would be arriving alongside the hydro mix shift rather than despite it, the FCF-CAGR-equivalent in net_gap_direction would be understated, and a real positive gap against the 5.3% implied ask would open. Single-legged and at the guide's own floor deliberately, so an in-line outcome tests the dive instead of confirming it.

earnings_quality.basis: The grade is NULL and the verdict is capped at WATCH because of it. Said plainly: the earnings-quality battery method section 7 defines CANNOT be computed for this issuer on the data this repo holds, and a grade that cannot be computed is NULL, never a default A or B. The missing input is deferred revenue and contract liabilities, and it is not a minor one here: ANDRITZ recognises revenue over time on long-cycle plant contracts funded by large customer advances (current liabilities of 4,887.7M EUR against current assets of 5,514.0M at 2025-12-31), so contract-liability drift is the single most diagnostic earnings-quality test for this business model, and the vendor aggregate at data/market/ANDR-VI.json carries no such line at all. Altman is separately PENDING_DATA (retained_earnings_fy missing, 7 of 8 inputs found); it is not one of section 7's veto inputs, but it is a second sign of how thin this balance-sheet plane is. WHAT THE MISSING INPUT IS NOT DOING: the cap does not rest on the absent datum alone. Of the four veto inputs that ARE computable, two are clean and two are flags. Clean: accruals at -2.34% of average total assets FY2025 (net income 456.3M against operating cash flow 652.7M over average assets of 8,386.55M), inside the 5% band and in the conservative direction, and FY2024 the same at -1.68%; Beneish M -2.42 against the -1.78 threshold, CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs. Flags: sustained DSO drift, 51.54 days (FY2022), 45.35 (FY2023), 51.31 (FY2024), 59.52 (FY2025), which is two consecutive years up to a four-year high while revenue fell 9.0% from its 2023 peak, receivables rising 19.5% as sales shrank; and two governance events inside eighteen months, an auditor change and a CFO change. Method section 7 puts sustained DSO drift in C territory on its own, so on the computable evidence the honest range is B-minus to C, not A. Capex to depreciation is unremarkable and rising modestly (0.613, 0.759, 0.794, 0.823 across FY2022-2025), below 1.0 throughout, consistent with an asset-light engineering model rather than with under-investment being used to flatter cash. Piotroski is 4 of 9, MIDDLING, on 9 of 9 inputs found, missing d_roa, d_leverage, d_current, shares and asset_turnover, which is a weak score for a name whose thesis is an upcycle and is consistent with a year in which revenue and net income both fell. Every number above is INFERRED from a vendor normalisation of statements this repo has never read, which is the T3 ceiling and is itself part of why the grade is NULL rather than a letter.

notes.text: TOO_LATE was seriously considered and not taken. The surface case for it is strong and is written out in what_is_priced_in and priced_in_summary rather than buried: +37.35% in twelve months, 100% of it multiple expansion, revenue and net income both down, price 0.72% off the 52-week high and at the sell-side average target. What stops it is that the multiple re-rated against genuinely new forward numbers (order intake +25.2%, backlog +20.5% to a record 1.60x revenue, hydro intake +81.8%), and for a plant engineer the order book is the estimate revision. That is correct pricing, not a story-driven re-rating, and method section 7's decomposition test does not support the call. Recorded here so the red team can attack the decision rather than reconstruct it.

This dive disagrees with its own upstream in one specific place and says so rather than inheriting it: the selection record calls this 'the widest gap of any COMPLETE candidate on this theme' on the strength of a 5.3% implied FCF CAGR against a hydro backlog up 15.3%. Built out like for like, the gap is +0.19 percentage points, inside the file's own 1.21-point horizon spread. The selection was not wrong to rank it first; the gap it described is smaller than it looked because it compared a segment growth rate to a group cash-flow rate, which is the category mismatch this analyst's red team has now flagged twice on other names.

Base-FCF check, run because the dive log requires it after the MYRG finding: base_fcf of 454.6M EUR is 1.088x the FY2022-2025 average of 417.9M, so this solve is NOT resting on an outlier year. The opposite caveat applies instead and is recorded in what_is_priced_in[3]: group FCF has compounded at -6.48% over three years, so the 5.3% ask is a trend reversal.
